question: Identify an OS service that ensures the efficient operation of the system itself.
scope_note: Final exam photos (Telegram.pdf p3-4).

question: Which of the following is NOT true about the operating system?
options: It is software that manages the computer hardware
It allows the user to process text and edit images
It provides an environment for application programs to run
It is the one program always running on the computer
scope_note: Marked D in source. B is clearly not an OS function (application software); D describes the kernel (part of the OS), so both B and D can be argued. Rewrite with one clear answer.

question: __________ means distributing subsets of data across multiple cores and carrying out the same operation on each.
Multithreading an interactive program will increase responsiveness to the user by:
options: continuing to run even if a part of it is blocked
asking the user to decide the order of multithreading
waiting for one part to finish before another begins
increasing the number of cores that run concurrently
scope_note: Duplicate concept of L08-29.

question: When a process is created using the classical fork() system call, which of the following is NOT inherited by the child process?
scope_note: Slides: each process has its own pid; child is a duplicate of the parent. User ID / open files inheritance is not covered.

question: The following are operating system goals EXCEPT:
options: Use the computer hardware in an efficient manner
Execute user programs and make solving user problems easier
Make the computer system convenient to use
scope_note: Midterm with graded answer sheet (p5). 5 options in source.

question: A(n) __________ is a software-generated interrupt caused either by an error or a user request.
scope_note: Correct term is 'trap' (or exception), which is not listed; the graded sheet marks the student's D wrong and writes 'trap'. Better rewritten with 'Trap' as an option.

question: When a user-level process wishes to call a function inside the kernel:
options: it directly executes the desired function
the OS changes it from user mode to kernel mode
the OS changes it from kernel mode to user mode

question: Each __________ is represented in the operating system by a __________.
In UNIX, which system call creates a new process?
scope_note: Student circled A; graded sheet corrects to C.

question: Why are APIs usually used more than system calls?
options: Because APIs are complex in calling
Because APIs show the details of the system calls
Because APIs run in kernel mode
scope_note: Slides say most details of the OS interface are hidden from the programmer by the API; portability is the textbook reason.

question: A(n) __________ occurs when a process could run but doesn't because other processes keep getting ahead of it.
The short-term scheduler, or CPU scheduler, selects from among the processes that are ____ to execute and allocates the ____ to ____ of them.

scope_note: Long-term scheduler is not in the slides.

question: Entering a __________ involves changing from __________ to __________.
options: Ready queue; running state; waiting state
System call; user mode; kernel mode

question: Which of the following about the parent-child process relation is NOT correct?
options: Parent and children may share all resources
Children may share a subset of the parent's resources
Children share the data and text segments with their parents
Parent and children may execute concurrently
scope_note: Source option letters were F-J; normalized. Student chose 'execute concurrently' and was marked wrong; the child is a duplicate with its own address space.

question: Which of the following can NOT be a state of a process?
A(n) __________ occurs when a short process waits because it comes after a long process.
When an I/O operation completes, the previously blocked process moves into the __________ state.
On a uniprocessor system, there is exactly one __________ process at any point in time.
What is the part of the operating system that is running all the time?
Five processes arrive together with CPU burst lengths 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 time units. What is the average waiting time using RR scheduling with a quantum of 9 units?
scope_note: q >= every burst, so RR behaves like FCFS: WT 0, 5, 11, 18, 26; avg = 12.

question: Which of the following algorithms has the same average waiting time as RR in the previous question?
scope_note: Bursts are already in increasing order and all arrive together, so FCFS, SJF and SRTF all give 12; the question has several correct answers. Student's 'A' was marked wrong. Rewrite before use.

question: Processes (arrival, burst): P1 (0, 5), P2 (1, 5), P3 (2, 4), P4 (3, 3). What is the total waiting time for P2 if SRTF scheduling is applied?
scope_note: P1 0-5 (never beaten), P4 5-8, P3 8-12, P2 12-17; WT(P2) = 17 - 1 - 5 = 11. Student circled A; graded sheet says D.

question: Same processes. The order of execution after applying the (nonpreemptive) SJF scheduling algorithm is:
scope_note: Student circled C; graded sheet says D.

question: Same processes. What would be the average waiting time if FCFS scheduling were applied?
Two threads run concurrently in the same program and both update a shared variable x (declared outside the thread functions, initial value 0). Variable x is allocated in the:
scope_note: Also ch4 s5 (threads share data).

question: In the same program, the loop variable j declared inside thread2() is allocated in the:
scope_note: Student circled A; graded sheet says B. Local variables live on each thread's own stack.

question: Program: cout<<"Hi"<<endl; fork(); cout<<"OK"<<endl; fork(); cout<<"Done"<<endl; Assume parents wait for their children. (1) How many processes are created? (2) What is the output?
answer: (1) 4 processes in total (3 newly created). (2) Hi printed once, OK twice, Done four times.
scope_note: State whether 'created' counts the original process when converting to MCQ.

question: Which of the following is NOT true about the short-term scheduler?
options: Selects which process should be executed next and allocates the CPU
Sometimes the only scheduler in a system
scope_note: Only the selection role is in the slides; the rest is textbook detail.

question: The role of the operating system is to:
options: provide basic computing resources (CPU, memory, I/O devices)
control and coordinate the use of hardware among various applications and users
define the ways in which the system resources are used to solve the computing problems of the users
perform specific tasks related to managing computer resources
scope_note: Option A = hardware, C = application programs (slide 5 wording).
